# Extracting data from PRISM (NY, CT, and NJ ZCTAs in 2024)

# You would want to change the following:
lines 44

```{r}
# ===========================================================
# 1. Packages
# ===========================================================

library(terra)
library(sf)
library(tigris)
library(exactextractr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(weathermetrics)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)


# ===========================================================
# 2. User settings
# ===========================================================

raster_dir <- "C:/Users/akg9010/Desktop/rasters"

dir.create(
  raster_dir,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

# Year(s) to process
years <- 2024

# States to include (two-letter USPS abbreviations)
states_of_interest <- c(
  "NY",
  "CT",
  "NJ"
)


# ===========================================================
# 3. Download GridMET files
# ===========================================================

download_gridmet <- function(variable, year) {
  
  outfile <- file.path(
    raster_dir,
    paste0(
      variable,
      "_",
      year,
      ".nc"
    )
  )
  
  if (!file.exists(outfile)) {
    
    message(
      "Downloading ",
      variable,
      " ",
      year
    )
    
    download.file(
      url = paste0(
        "https://www.northwestknowledge.net/metdata/data/",
        variable,
        "_",
        year,
        ".nc"
      ),
      destfile = outfile,
      mode = "wb"
    )
    
  } else {
    
    message(
      "File already exists: ",
      outfile
    )
    
  }
}


# Download maximum temperature
walk(
  years,
  ~download_gridmet(
    "tmmx",
    .x
  )
)


# Download maximum relative humidity
walk(
  years,
  ~download_gridmet(
    "rmax",
    .x
  )
)


# ===========================================================
# 4. Load ALL US ZCTAs
# ===========================================================

message(
  "Loading 2020 US ZCTAs..."
)

zcta_all <- zctas(
  year = 2020
) %>%
  st_transform(4326)


# ===========================================================
# 5. Load state boundaries for states of interest
# ===========================================================

message(
  "Loading state boundaries for: ",
  paste(
    states_of_interest,
    collapse = ", "
  )
)

states_boundary <- states(
  cb = FALSE,
  year = 2020
) %>%
  filter(
    STUSPS %in% states_of_interest
  ) %>%
  st_transform(4326)


# ===========================================================
# 6. Identify ZCTAs that fall within the states of interest
# ===========================================================

message(
  "Identifying ZCTAs within states of interest..."
)

# Use a representative point within each ZCTA (rather than the
# true centroid, which can fall outside oddly-shaped polygons)
# so each ZCTA is assigned to exactly one state.

zcta_points <- st_point_on_surface(
  zcta_all
)

zcta_points_joined <- st_join(
  zcta_points,
  states_boundary["STUSPS"],
  join = st_within
)

zcta_state_lookup <- zcta_points_joined %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(STUSPS)
  ) %>%
  select(
    ZCTA5CE20,
    STUSPS
  )


# ===========================================================
# 7. Select requested ZCTAs (with polygon geometry retained)
# ===========================================================

target_zcta <- zcta_all %>%
  filter(
    ZCTA5CE20 %in% zcta_state_lookup$ZCTA5CE20
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    zcta_state_lookup,
    by = "ZCTA5CE20"
  )

target_zctas <- as.character(
  target_zcta$ZCTA5CE20
)


# ===========================================================
# 8. Clean ZCTA geometries
# ===========================================================

message(
  "Cleaning ZCTA geometries..."
)

target_zcta <- st_make_valid(
  target_zcta
)


# Keep polygon and multipolygon geometries only

target_zcta <- target_zcta[
  st_geometry_type(target_zcta) %in%
    c(
      "POLYGON",
      "MULTIPOLYGON"
    ),
]


# ===========================================================
# 9. Summarize selected ZCTAs
# ===========================================================

found_zctas <- sort(
  unique(
    as.character(
      target_zcta$ZCTA5CE20
    )
  )
)

message(
  "Number of ZCTAs selected: ",
  length(found_zctas)
)

message(
  "ZCTAs per state:"
)

print(
  target_zcta %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    count(
      STUSPS,
      name = "n_zctas"
    ) %>%
    arrange(
      STUSPS
    )
)

# Lookup table of ZCTA -> state, to attach to the final output
zcta_state_lookup_final <- target_zcta %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(
    ZCTA = ZCTA5CE20,
    STATE = STUSPS
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ZCTA = as.character(ZCTA)
  )


# ===========================================================
# 10. Function to process one year
# ===========================================================

process_year <- function(year) {
  
  message(
    "=========================================="
  )
  
  message(
    "Processing year ",
    year
  )
  
  message(
    "=========================================="
  )
  
  
  # =========================================================
  # Load maximum temperature raster
  # =========================================================
  
  message(
    "Loading temperature raster..."
  )
  
  tmax <- rast(
    file.path(
      raster_dir,
      paste0(
        "tmmx_",
        year,
        ".nc"
      )
    )
  )
  
  
  # =========================================================
  # Load relative humidity raster
  # =========================================================
  
  message(
    "Loading humidity raster..."
  )
  
  rh <- rast(
    file.path(
      raster_dir,
      paste0(
        "rmax_",
        year,
        ".nc"
      )
    )
  )
  
  
  # =========================================================
  # Extract mean daily maximum temperature
  # =========================================================
  
  message(
    "Extracting daily maximum temperature..."
  )
  
  tmax_extract <- exact_extract(
    tmax,
    target_zcta,
    "mean",
    progress = TRUE
  )
  
  
  # =========================================================
  # Extract mean daily maximum relative humidity
  # =========================================================
  
  message(
    "Extracting daily maximum relative humidity..."
  )
  
  rh_extract <- exact_extract(
    rh,
    target_zcta,
    "mean",
    progress = TRUE
  )
  
  
  # =========================================================
  # Convert extraction results to data frames
  # =========================================================
  
  tmax_extract <- as.data.frame(
    tmax_extract
  )
  
  rh_extract <- as.data.frame(
    rh_extract
  )
  
  
  # =========================================================
  # Rename raster layers
  # =========================================================
  
  names(tmax_extract) <-
    paste0(
      "day_",
      seq_len(
        ncol(tmax_extract)
      )
    )
  
  names(rh_extract) <-
    paste0(
      "day_",
      seq_len(
        ncol(rh_extract)
      )
    )
  
  
  # =========================================================
  # Add ZCTA
  # =========================================================
  
  tmax_extract$ZCTA <-
    as.character(
      target_zcta$ZCTA5CE20
    )
  
  rh_extract$ZCTA <-
    as.character(
      target_zcta$ZCTA5CE20
    )
  
  
  # =========================================================
  # Long format temperature
  # =========================================================
  
  tmax_long <-
    tmax_extract %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = starts_with("day_"),
      names_to = "day",
      values_to = "tmax_k"
    )
  
  
  # =========================================================
  # Long format humidity
  # =========================================================
  
  rh_long <-
    rh_extract %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = starts_with("day_"),
      names_to = "day",
      values_to = "rh"
    )
  
  
  # =========================================================
  # Combine temperature and humidity
  # =========================================================
  
  output <-
    left_join(
      tmax_long,
      rh_long,
      by = c(
        "ZCTA",
        "day"
      )
    ) %>%
    
    mutate(
      
      # -----------------------------------------------------
      # Convert day_1, day_2, etc. to day number
      # -----------------------------------------------------
      
      day =
        as.integer(
          gsub(
            "day_",
            "",
            day
          )
        ),
      
      
      # -----------------------------------------------------
      # Create calendar date
      # -----------------------------------------------------
      
      date =
        as.Date(
          paste0(
            year,
            "-01-01"
          )
        ) +
        day - 1,
      
      
      # -----------------------------------------------------
      # GridMET tmmx is in Kelvin
      # Convert Kelvin to Celsius
      # -----------------------------------------------------
      
      tmax_c =
        tmax_k - 273.15,
      
      
      # -----------------------------------------------------
      # Cap relative humidity at 100%
      #
      # GridMET's rmax layer is model-derived (not a direct
      # measurement), so area-weighted means can come out
      # slightly above 100% (e.g., 100.2%) even though relative
      # humidity is physically capped at 100%. This matters
      # because weathermetrics::heat.index() treats ANY rh > 100
      # as an "impossible value" and silently sets heat index to
      # NA for that row -- so without this fix, days that are
      # effectively saturated (rh == 100) can end up dropped as
      # NA instead of getting a valid heat index. Clamping to
      # [0, 100] here keeps those rows and calculates heat index
      # correctly.
      # -----------------------------------------------------
      
      rh =
        pmin(
          pmax(
            rh,
            0
          ),
          100
        ),
      
      
      # -----------------------------------------------------
      # Calculate Heat Index
      # NOTE: weathermetrics::heat.index() has its own internal
      # "round" argument, which defaults to round = 1. If left
      # at the default, the value is truncated to 1 decimal
      # place *inside* the function, before it ever reaches the
      # outer round() call below -- so the outer rounding can't
      # recover the lost precision. To get a true 2-decimal-place
      # result, we tell heat.index() itself to keep 2 decimals,
      # and match the outer round() to the same precision.
      #
      # Because this is built from tmmx (daily maximum
      # temperature) and rmax (daily maximum relative humidity),
      # this heat index represents each ZCTA's daily MAX heat
      # index.
      # -----------------------------------------------------
      
      heat_index_c =
        round(
          heat.index(
            t = tmax_c,
            rh = rh,
            temperature.metric = "celsius",
            round = 2
          ),
          digits = 2
        ),
      
      
      # -----------------------------------------------------
      # Add year
      # -----------------------------------------------------
      
      year = year
      
    ) %>%
    
    
    # =======================================================
    # Keep final variables
    # =======================================================
    
    select(
      ZCTA,
      date,
      year,
      tmax_c,
      rh,
      heat_index_c
    )
  
  
  return(
    output
  )
}


# ===========================================================
# 11. Run all years
# ===========================================================

message(
  "Starting processing for ",
  length(target_zctas),
  " ZCTAs (",
  paste(
    states_of_interest,
    collapse = ", "
  ),
  ") and years ",
  min(years),
  "-",
  max(years)
)


target_zcta_heat_index <-
  
  map_dfr(
    years,
    process_year
  )


# ===========================================================
# 12. Make sure ZCTA remains character, attach state
# ===========================================================

target_zcta_heat_index$ZCTA <-
  as.character(
    target_zcta_heat_index$ZCTA
  )

target_zcta_heat_index <-
  target_zcta_heat_index %>%
  left_join(
    zcta_state_lookup_final,
    by = "ZCTA"
  ) %>%
  relocate(
    STATE,
    .after = ZCTA
  )


# ===========================================================
# 13. Save as RDS
# ===========================================================

saveRDS(
  target_zcta_heat_index,
  file.path(
    raster_dir,
    "ny_ct_nj_zcta_heat_index_2024.rds"
  )
)


# ===========================================================
# 14. Save as CSV
# ===========================================================

write.csv(
  target_zcta_heat_index,
  file.path(
    raster_dir,
    "ny_ct_nj_zcta_heat_index_2024.csv"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

```
